newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas drifts lower on short-term weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas drifts lower on short-term weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices erased earlier gains Thursday, pressured by mild weather forecasts and a lower storage injection demand, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices were in opposition again to April gas futures, as cash fell by about 10 cents to an average range of $1.78-1.832 per mmBtu. Henry Hub was quoted in the low-$1.80s.
NYMEX's Henry Hub April gas futures at 1324 EST was 6.1 cents higher at $1.90.
In the East, swing prices in the Appalachian region tumbled into the $1.90s, down nearly 10 cents from Wednesday's levels.

At the New York city-gate, prices hovered around $2.20, supported by forecasts for cooler air Friday in the Northeast. In its six-to-10 day forecast, the National Weather Service is calling for more below-normal temperatures next week.
In the Midcontinent, prices eroded into the mid-$1.70s, down seven cents from Wednesday's trading range. Chicago city-gate was quoted in the mid-$1.90s, losing about 10 cents.
Temperatures in the Midwest are forecast to hover near to slightly above normal through early next week, except in parts of the northern plains where cold weather continues.
In the Permian basin, gas prices were down more than 10 cents to the high-$1.60s to low-$1.70s.
Southern California border prices slipped into the high-$1.70s to mid-$1.80s, though deals were reported done in a wide range of $1.70-1.84.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California is still scheduled to restart around March 12 following repairs of a leak, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.

American Gas Association said Wednesday that last week's gas stocks were down 76 bcf to 988 bcf, or 31 percent of capacity. In the producing region, where stocks have been the most depleted, inventories were 11 bcf lower at 237 bcf, or 26 percent full.
